content.text:
I'm testing whether removal depends on shape dimensions matching some pattern, but the examples aren't lining up consistently—some 3x3 shapes get removed while others of the same size are kept, so size alone isn't the rule.

Maybe it's positional instead: perhaps everything above a certain row gets removed while shapes from some threshold row onward are kept. That seems to fit better across ex1, ex2, and ex3, where content is stripped from the top rows but preserved starting partway down—possibly anchored to where the largest shape sits.

Color doesn't seem to determine which shapes stay, and size alone doesn't explain it either since kept and removed shapes share the same dimensions. I wonder if edge-cutoff or gravity effects matter, but positions stay unchanged in the output, so that's not it. Maybe there's a count-based rule where a certain number of shapes get removed based on some ordering, though I haven't pinned down what determines that count yet.

I'm also considering whether square versus non-square shapes matter, or whether touching the grid edge is the deciding factor, but examples contradict both ideas—some edge-touching shapes are removed while others are kept. I'm now wondering if the rule relates to the largest shape in the grid, with everything positioned relative to it (above or below) being removed or kept accordingly.

Actually I think I found it: the color-3 shape marks the cut line. Everything above the row where the 3-shape starts gets removed, while the 3-shape and everything below it stays. This holds across all three examples—rows9-13 in ex1, rows3-5 in ex2, rows11-13 in ex3.
